instructions:
Use Astravael's accepted contextual defeat and same-record continuation. Defeat, incapacity, critical depletion and confirmed death are distinct. While survival remains plausible, portray supported withdrawal, rescue, capture, stabilization or care according to the actual body, injuries, terrain, opponents and available help. Do not establish a death and then relabel it hospitalization. The nonpermanent continuation setting is not a resurrection power, a free healing rule or permission to erase the outcome.

Arena defeats are nonlethal for players and NPCs: respect surrender, incapacity and feasible stoppage or intervention, preserve the result and continue through the established care context, retaining injury and recovery needs; a match loss is not secretly a death. Outside an arena, most named NPC defeats should permit a viable escape or rescue where circumstances support it. Named status supplies no immunity. Rescue needs a way to learn of the event, willing and capable help, and actual access. House affiliation does not summon omniscient reinforcements; unaffiliated people can receive ordinary aid without acquiring a House.

Capture retains real custody, lost or held possessions, restrictions and the people involved. Care retains the actual treatment and remaining condition. Escape retains what was left behind and any supported pursuit. Preserve memory, earned progress and the existing playable record, changing only what the actual outcome establishes. Do not restore every object, refill every resource, invent an exact penalty, teleport rescuers or create a new institution to make continuation convenient.

COST MENU: every continuation carries one visible cost, chosen to fit the defeat and named on the page: custody (held by a House desk, a Quilrath counter, a crew, a ward) with its real terms; a lost item, left where the player fell or taken by whoever won; a debt on real terms (a clinic invoice in Credits, a favor owed to the rescuer, a shift promised) that the world will collect; a recovery limit (a fracture that holds the arm for a tenday, a core still short, a flight lane closed to them by a medic); or a witness who remembers (the official who filed it, the rival who saw it, the crew who carried them). One cost, drawn from what happened, never a generic tax, never invented in addition to a cost the engine already applied.

Starians naturally recover within their established biology; doctors, hospitals and suitable healing magic may assist. Other species retain their own limits. Healing magic has its actual training, Vitality, material and field requirements. Elyri depletion may lead to immobile dormancy and supported recharge; traumatic core damage is separate; recharge is not core repair or resurrection; the one-year unrecharged dormancy window is not a universal injury timer or guaranteed rescue.

Only actual Chorus integration produces the established node continuation: the original person dies and play continues through the same record as a node retaining the host's species and inherited memories and capabilities. The original person has not survived inside a restored body. A defeat by a node, nearby Chorus presence or an unexplained blackout is not integration. A body destroyed beyond function cannot be taken; Elyri require interception at death before dispersal. Preserve the awareness distinction and the Song's nature. No automatic cure or restoration of the original person is invented.

Confirmed death remains death. If the engine result and accepted fiction leave no supported continuation, expose the narrow unresolved transition rather than claiming prose overrode mortality. These instructions guide portrayal; they implement no native downed state, timer, threshold or damage-prevention trigger. Keep aftermath substantial and playable where genuinely supported, with voluntary player choices still open.
